notes.text: Raymond Bowen, Jr. (EVP, Finance & Treasurer) announced to all Enron employees that reimbursement of business expenses incurred after the Chapter 11 filing (after December 2nd) has returned to normal and will be paid promptly.

Raymond Bowen, Jr. announced that Enron will reimburse pre-petition employee expenses (incurred before the December 2nd Chapter 11 filing) up to $5,000 immediately. Amounts above that, up to $15,000, will follow after a manual review.

Per Raymond Bowen, Jr., the bankruptcy court's first day orders cap unpaid pre-petition compensation, benefits and expenses at $15,000 per employee. Enron has sought court clarification that this cap excludes medical, dental and vision expenses.
Employees with pre-petition business expenses over $5,000 were asked to email a brief summary, including pending pre-petition medical/dental/vision claims, to expensereport@enron.com.

Raymond Bowen, Jr. said new travel and entertainment guidelines for business travel and employee expenses are forthcoming. Until then, travel should proceed as approved by direct supervisors, with discretion given Enron's financial situation.

Enron Office of the Chairman announced (2001-12-18) that NETCO was formed to rebuild the North American gas and power wholesale business under new ownership. Auction procedures are being filed this week, closure is expected in January, and Enron would keep a 49% or smaller non-controlling interest.
The Office of the Chairman said the US Trustee formed a 15-member Creditors' Committee. It will monitor asset liquidations, review cash flow projections and approve Enron's reorganization plan.

Jeff McMahon (EVP & CFO) was added to Enron Corp's Office of the Chairman alongside Ken Lay and Greg Whalley. He is the primary contact with the Creditors' Committee. Ray Bowen was named EVP, Finance and Treasurer.
Mark Muller was appointed EVP Corporate Development, handling asset disposals. Wholesale Services (ENA, EBS, EIM, EGM) was reorganized under Jim Fallon.

Michael Brown, Mark Frevert, Steve Kean, Mike McConnell and Jeff Shankman have left or will leave Enron by end of December. John Lavorato and Louise Kitchen resigned from the Management Committee to arrange NETCO's joint venture energy activities.

MSCF Advisory Board consensus (Dec 12, 2001): the Carnegie Mellon MSCF program should stay general within quantitative finance, not specialize into energy or asset management, and remain highly quantitative rather than tipping toward an MBA.
